title: The kernel keeps records of its own
reason: Built and reviewed on the unmerged stack. Sessions, jobs, the replay store and the action log all keep their rows here, so nothing in waves 2, 4 or 5 starts until it is on dev. The work left is review and merge.
state_evidence: Not in dev's src/; all four landings built on stacked unmerged branches ending at origin/the-kernel-writes-records-behind-and-sweeps-them (56 ahead of dev), each review 'lands'.
risk_note: On SQLite, records queue behind a batch; behind a writer held over ~20 s a session change can land without its record.
outcome: The kernel gets one durable place, in the database the root mount already uses, to keep sessions, jobs and later the action log, without making reads wait.
technical: Adds a private vfs.kernel_store on the root storage's place (RecordPlace, record_place): same SQLite file on its own connections, same Postgres database on its own pool, memory for an in-memory root. Provides tables at first use, a bounded write-behind buffer, record-after-change transactions, counters, chunked helpers, sweep of expired rows, and close semantics with a Deadline.
surface_note: Adds RecordPlace and Storage.record_place; sweep removes expired records; the rest is private.
open_decisions: Records in the mount's own SQLite file (ruled; price is queuing behind batches)
Own Postgres pool of the mount's size (ruled)
A store of another format is refused, never reset

title: Concurrent writes on Postgres outlive their retries
reason: Measured: about one in seventy single-file writes is refused when 32 sessions write at once on Postgres. That is the production engine at the reference deployment's own concurrency. The roadmap does not list it. A pilot would hit it in the first hour.
state_evidence: Status: draft, nothing built; contended row not yet identified; listed under K2's drafts in the roadmap.
risk_note: The contended row is unknown; the fix may touch directory aggregates.
outcome: 32 agents writing new files into separate directories on Postgres are all served. Today about one write in seventy fails with a conflict even though they share no file.
technical: Log serialization failures' relation under REPEATABLE READ to find the shared row (suspect: the parent directory or its aggregate), then remove the contention or coalesce it and resize the four-attempt retry. Also a pool-sizing sentence for 32 concurrent batches.
open_decisions: Which row the writes share

title: A mount with `schema=` on Postgres makes its schema at first touch when it is absent, and a role that may not make it is refused `unavailable` naming the schema and the privilege, never `internal`
reason: The first thing an enterprise does is point vfs at a schema with a restricted role. Today that answers internal. It should create the schema or name the missing privilege.

The kernel store makes the schema the same way; SQLite and the floor send no schema statement.
surface_note: Changes the error kind and data keys a privilege failure returns (internal -> unavailable, retryable false, data.schema, data.privilege).

title: Postgres reads a subtree by its range, and searches vectors through its index
reason: Every subtree call on Postgres scans the whole table today. At ten million files and 150,000 calls a day that is the single largest cost in the design. The roadmap does not gate it. It also removes a public option, so it belongs before the freeze.
state_evidence: Status line: nothing built; descendant_filter is still a bound LIKE (descent.py:202); ivfflat still in src/vfs/models/vector.py; native_ann still served below pgvector 0.8 (backend.py:663). Roadmap storage table: 'none is a gate item'.
risk_note: Touches the subtree predicate used by move and delete; recall measured only on synthetic 128-dim vectors.
outcome: A subtree read on Postgres costs what the subtree holds on every connection, even after asyncpg switches to a generic plan. Vector search on Postgres returns the depth it asks for, with recall pinned by a test.
technical: descendant_filter becomes the bytewise range path > root||'/' AND path < root||'0' on both tuned engines (LIKE kept on the floor), affecting move, delete, posture walks, meta exclusion and tree. native_ann is served only on pgvector 0.8+; index_method='ivfflat' is removed; a Postgres below the oldest supported major is refused at first touch.
surface_note: Removes index_method='ivfflat'; adds a first-touch refusal for Postgres below 15.
open_decisions: Below pgvector 0.8: serve the exact tier, or set hnsw.ef_search to the depth?
Remove ivfflat, or build its index once data exists?

title: The topology lock is held for a commit
reason: It breaks the project's own rule that a lock other callers need is held only for a commit, and the replay store waits on it. Do the cheap relabel fix now and run the spike for the late lock.
state_evidence: serialized.py:112 serialize() docstring: 'always the verb's first statement'; called first in trash.py and topology.py; labels.py relabel update has no everyone_level <> rank term.
risk_note: Taking the lock last needs a re-check per verb that is not yet known; both defects were read, not run.
outcome: A large delete, restore, move or copy no longer blocks every other such verb on the mount for the whole batch. Relabels stop rewriting rows that are already right.
technical: serialize() moves from the verb's first statement to its last before commit, with earlier reads re-checked under the lock (found by a spike). relabel_spans gains everyone_level <> :rank.

title: A connection lost during COMMIT answers vfs.unavailable.in_doubt, retry class refresh, and is never redriven
reason: A commit that loses its connection must never read as a failure that is safe to retry. It stands alone, needs nothing, and is the first step of the replay chain.
state_evidence: Status line: draft, not reviewed, nothing built; no 'in_doubt' in src; state-on-dev 177-2 still-needed.
risk_note: Draws 'in doubt' wide (every DBAPI or OS error at commit), so some recoverable failures become read-first; a merge with the engine-core split branch is needed.
outcome: A caller whose change lost its connection at commit is told the change may or may not have landed and to read before retrying. vfs never silently runs the change twice.
technical: Wraps the one commit call in the mutation runner with seams; a failure there that is not a transient refusal answers the new child kind vfs.unavailable.in_doubt, retry class refresh, not retryable, with no redrive. A loss inside a statement stays vfs.unavailable.backend.
surface_note: Adds error kind vfs.unavailable.in_doubt and retry class refresh on it; data key in_doubt: true shared with the jobs spec.
open_decisions: Where the in-doubt line is drawn (taken: every non-transient commit failure)
Kind vs data key in_doubt for calls with their own answer, shared with the jobs spec
Whether the hint later names request_key

title: Grep reads a pattern as its matcher does
reason: Grep silently drops matches today: one word-boundary pattern finds 6 files where ripgrep finds 421, and a character-class pattern finds none of 751. Agents trust grep more than any other verb. At minimum refuse the patterns it cannot serve.
state_evidence: Status line says nothing is built; the gate _gate is still Python sre-based in src/vfs/pattern_matching/grep.py:260 and the fold still uses str.casefold (src/vfs/models/code_grams.py, indexing.py).
risk_note: The interim refusal is small; the HIR walk and fold table are engine work, and a fold change forces a rebuild of every existing index.
outcome: A database grep never silently drops a row its matcher would return. Today \<kmalloc returns 6 files where rg returns 421, and [[:alpha:]]_count returns 0 where rg returns 751, with no warning.
technical: Short term, the language gate refuses as invalid the constructs Python sre and the Rust regex crate read differently (\<, \>, \b{...}, POSIX and nested classes). Long term, the gram plan walks the regex-syntax HIR in crates/vfs-core, the index fold becomes a Rust table generated from the matcher's Unicode case tables, and the fold's Unicode version is stored with the index generation so a mismatch reads as stale.
surface_note: Decision 2 makes some grep patterns refused as invalid until the HIR walk lands; decision 4 changes index staleness; a fold change forces one full rebuild.
open_decisions: Refuse the diverging constructs now, or build the HIR walk first and refuse nothing
A stale fold serves every row from the scan side until rebuild, or grep refuses on a stale index

title: A shell line has one admission budget and one terminal outcome
reason: Measured on dev: a line given a 0.3 second deadline ended at 4.06 seconds, and a line can report success after an interpreter limit has run out. A deadline that does not bound the call is a defect in a shipped verb, and it must be closed before the shell is served over the wire. The roadmap does not list it.
state_evidence: src/vfs/shell/host.py run_line passes deadline.remaining() at construction and awaits host.answer() with no timeout; verification.md measured a 0.3 s deadline ending at 4.06 s.
risk_note: Settling an in-flight commit on both engines under cancel, plus fork-safety of native objects, needs controlled seams and real-engine tests.
outcome: A shell line honours its deadline even while a storage call is slow, and a line that hits an interpreter limit never reports success. Every caller sees the one stop that actually happened: timeout, cancel, budget or normal end.
technical: A shared line control (absolute monotonic deadline plus cancel flag) created before queueing; deadline rechecked around every verb await and before each batched request; first fatal stop wins and latches in background jobs. Shell-owned native buffers charged to memory_bytes; fuel validated as an integer in range; typed startup causes keep 2/124/130/137; a forked child gets a fresh pool, engine and ticker.
surface_note: Changes the meaning of exit codes 124/130/137 and success on cli/run_line at the edges; documents that a committed write may coexist with a timeout.

title: The shell matches patterns and regular expressions in time linear in the text
reason: A crafted pattern can burn a line's whole budget. It is cheap, changes no name, and should be closed before the shell is reachable over the wire in wave 3.
state_evidence: Status line says nothing is built; regex.rs is still a backtracking walk under STEP_BUDGET; pattern.rs already memoizes (node, position), unclear whether that covers decision 2.
risk_note: Pike simulation cost on ordinary patterns is not measured; contained in two engine files.
outcome: No pattern an agent writes can make the shell's matcher burn its whole budget or fail where bash answers at once. Pathological globs and regexes answer in milliseconds.

title: A keyed mutation commits its answer with its change and a resend gets that answer back
reason: This is what makes a retry safe: a call sent twice with the same key applies once and returns the first answer. Agents retry constantly and so do networks. The interrupt design reuses the same store.
state_evidence: Status line: draft, not reviewed, nothing built; no request_key or replayed kind in src; state-on-dev 177-3 still-needed.

outcome: A caller that lost a reply can resend the same call with the same key and get the original answer back, without the change running twice. This makes every retry safe and gives approvals a resumption token.
technical: A per-mount replay store (new replays.py) keeps the fingerprinted call's compressed Result in the same transaction as the change, paged by BLOB_PAGE_BYTES; a hit returns it with one vfs.replayed info record and no mutation. Adds a replay storage trait, retention and reclaim.
surface_note: Adds error kind vfs.replayed with fields first_at/expires_at, the replay storage trait, and a key validator; public request_key argument itself is 177-4.

title: `read` checks every body it serves against its recorded hash and refuses a mismatched, missing or unhashed body with `vfs.unavailable.integrity`, unless the caller asks for the salvage read
reason: A body changed outside vfs reads as success today. For an enterprise, a store that cannot say its data was tampered with is not a governed store. Four other specs wait on it.
state_evidence: Status line: nothing built; state-on-dev 175-1 still-needed; no content_digest, read_check or unavailable.integrity in src.

outcome: A body changed, deleted or stripped of its hash underneath vfs (for example by an ETL job with raw SQL) reads as one never-retryable integrity error instead of a silent success. A caller can still salvage the bytes with read(verify=False).
technical: Adds content_digest and moves the per-call offload rule to vfs/offload.py; adds ErrorKind.integrity as vfs.unavailable.integrity with a fixed data record. A fault is believed only when two reads in two transactions agree (redrive through the retry layer); new integrity modules shrink reads.py; storage declares a read_check trait; grep and search stay unverified.

title: Every written file reports its recorded hash, and replacing a damaged body preserves the evidence
